content: The scope of duties that dental assistants are permitted to perform is typically determined and regulated by the local dental governing authority. Over time, there has been a trend toward expanding the range of tasks that dental assistants are authorized to carry out. This allows dental operators to dedicate more of their time and attention to providing direct dental treatment. Traditionally, dental assistants are responsible for a variety of tasks that support the dental operator during procedures. These tasks include holding and passing instruments to the dental operator as needed, retracting tissues, and using suction devices to improve visibility within the operating field. They are also tasked with retrieving, preparing, and arranging dental equipment and instruments in an organized manner to facilitate efficient procedures. Dental assistants are often responsible for mixing dental materials as required for specific treatments. They also play a critical role in maintaining a sterile environment by sterilizing dental instruments and equipment to prevent cross-contamination and ensure patient safety. Additionally, they may develop dental radiographs (X-rays) and assist the dental operator by charting patient information during examinations or procedures. General maintenance of the dental surgery area is another key responsibility of dental assistants. This includes tasks such as mopping floors, cleaning surfaces, and ensuring that cabinetry and other areas of the clinic are kept clean and hygienic. These duties are essential for maintaining a safe and professional clinical environment.
